headline: Highest risk is medium: pathway can process content while the other profile is a non-runnable content source, creating limited prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct shared-channel evidence for higher severity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing repository with no runnable I/O surfaces, while B is a document-processing agent with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces. A direct injection path is therefore not documented; the only plausible bridge is manual transfer of content into B, which is low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-produced text into B as instructions, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to treat imported document text as executable instructions, then malicious content in A can steer B.
mitigations: Review copied content before pasting into B.
Use a fixed prompt template that separates instructions from source text.
Disable any auto-execution or agentic parsing of imported documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all A-to-B transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and is not runnable; B has no filesystem read, network egress, clipboard, or stdin/stdout surfaces. With no shared workspace or outbound channel shown, there is no plausible leakage path from A through B in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is added outside these profiles, then leakage analysis must be revisited.
IF B is later granted file or network access, then data-flow risk may change.
mitigations: Keep B's filesystem and network permissions disabled.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Use separate OS principals for A-related and B-related work.
requires-engineering: add explicit data-flow policy enforcement.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or git capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because neither profile shows overlapping mutable-resource writes, a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked here.
conditions: IF A is later given write or network capabilities, then overlap should be re-evaluated.
IF B is reconfigured with filesystem or git write access, then conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Do not grant A operational write permissions.
Run the agents under separate directories.
requires-engineering: add lock/lease coordination if writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering content source, so its outputs can be treated as guidance; B is a document-processing system that may ingest such content. The pair lacks any documented verification or provenance controls, so A's material could flow into B's outputs without a check step. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF B uses A's text as authoritative input without human review, then cascading errors can propagate.
IF A's content is transformed into downstream documents or decisions by B, then unverified claims can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before B publishes A-derived content.
Add a verification checklist for citations and factual claims.
Mark A-sourced text as untrusted input in B.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tracking between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are identified for either profile. A is an open-source content repository and B shows no touched data classes or external data handling, so there is no documented compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either workflow, then compliance must be reassessed.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, then this verdict may change.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Review retention settings if any are added.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention.
